CPU path: Auto draws each bucket of batches (one pipeline state and vertex arena) with one indirect call where the device has multiDrawIndirect and drawIndirectFirstInstance, else with a direct draw per batch; PerDraw always draws per batch. GPU path: Auto draws each bucket with one drawIndexedIndirectCount where the device has drawIndirectCount, NoCount with one drawIndexedIndirect over the bucket's draw slots (those the GPU did not fill have no instances), PerDraw with one drawIndexedIndirect per slot (also without multiDrawIndirect). Tests set it low to check the splits. |

Changes of proxies already on the GPU always upload at once. |
| `VisibilityFeedback` | `bool` | `true` | GPU-driven frames take their asset requests (and the screen sizes texture streaming follows) from the GPU's visibility feedback of a frame two or three frames earlier instead of walking the view's proxies on the CPU: what each mesh and material is used for, in the view (above HighPriorityScreenFraction or not), within PrefetchDistance or casting shadows. The CPU's marks still run on a renderer's first frames, after camera cuts (TextureStreamingPolicy:\:IsCameraCut), and after a frame whose draws overflowed the slots the feedback foresaw; meshes of unknown bounds, transparent surfaces and skinned proxies are always the CPU's. Off: the CPU's marks every frame. |
| `OcclusionCulling` | `bool` | `true` | GPU-driven frames leave out of the view what lies behind what the view draws, in two phases: the first draws what was visible in the previous frame into the depth prepass, a depth pyramid of that (Scene/HZBBuild.comp) tests every other proxy in the frustum, and the second phase draws those found visible (in the same frame: nothing appears a frame late). Camera cuts and a renderer's first frame start without history (the first phase draws nothing). The shadow cascades are culled alike, each against a pyramid of its own first phase's shadow map (a quarter of the cascades' size each way): casters hidden from the light behind other casters are left out. That costs GPU time of its own, so it runs while it pays: while the latest frame that culled the cascades found at least a sixteenth of their casters hidden, otherwise once every 16 frames to look again (SceneRendererStats:\:ShadowOcclusionCulled). |
| `MinimumSamplerPyramids` | `bool` | `true` | The depth pyramids occlusion culling tests against are built with a minimum-filtering sampler where the device has one (GraphicsDeviceInfo:\:SupportsSamplerMinMax): one sample per 2x2 texels. False builds them with four loads per 2x2 on every device, as devices without one do: tests compare them. |
| `CacheShadowCascades` | `bool` | `true` | GPU-driven frames redraw a shadow cascade only when something that reaches it changed since the frame that drew it: the camera (any part of SceneCamera or the viewport), the light or the cascade's square, a caster whose bounds before or after its change reach the cascade (a caster's first change, the frames before which it was not followed, redraws every cascade), or what the casters are drawn with (the scene's GPU copy's mesh and material tables, the geometry pool's tables and, while materials are alpha-masked, the texture table's entries). Other cascades keep their shadow map layer (SceneRendererStats:\:CachedCascadeMask): a still camera over a still or local change costs no shadow draws. |
| `TemporalAntiAliasing` | `bool` | `true` | Scenes whose PostProcessComponent chooses AntiAliasingMode:\:TAA are drawn with temporal anti-aliasing: each frame offsets its samples by a sub-pixel jitter (8 phases of a Halton (2, 3) sequence, from the history's latest reset on, in the frame's copy of the camera only: culling, levels of detail, the shadow cascades and the overlays keep the camera's own matrices) and blends with the renderer's history of earlier frames. The history is the renderer's own and starts again (SceneRendererStats:\:HistoryResets) on its first frame, after a camera cut, with a render scene that is neither the previous one nor a clone of it, after a resize, after a device frame (Renderer:\:GetFrameNumber) in which it did not render, and after ResetHistory. Off: such scenes are drawn with FXAA (renderers of single images that do not render a view several times, such as thumbnails). |

The last pass that writes the display image dithers it (the tone mapping, or FXAA after it); the overlays and the copy into a target are exact display colors. Tests that compare exact pixels turn it off (Tests:\:ExactSpecification). |

SpecularEnergyCompensation: the forward pass scales specular light by GetSpecularEnergy (Include/PBR.slang), which restores what single scattering loses on rough surfaces; off, the specular light is the single-scattering lobe's. HorizonFade: reflections a normal map turns into the surface fade out (GetHorizonFade); off, they do not. Both reach the forward pass as FrameConstants:\:CaptureSwitches bits (a uniform branch, nothing while 0). SpatialReflectionResolve: the spatial screen-space reflections' 5x5 resolve (Effects/ReflectionResolve.comp); off, the forward pass reads each pixel's traced reflection as the march found it. |
